config.theme: Family video call planning a cousin's wedding
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Family video call planning a cousin's wedding

personas.name: Carmen
personas.role: Mother of the bride, runs the call
personas.hidden_agenda: Wants to invite her whole church group

personas.name: Nina
personas.goals: Keep it small and on budget
personas.hidden_agenda: Quietly wants to drop the formal dinner for a taco truck

personas.name: Dani
personas.hidden_agenda: Has been covering small costs out of pocket

personas.name: Leo
personas.role: Cousin, in charge of music and the shuttle
personas.hidden_agenda: Already promised his band could play a set

pack.title: Nina and Sam's wedding - family planning call

agenda.title: Guest list and RSVPs
agenda.goal: Get a real headcount and chase missing RSVPs

agenda.title: Venue and catering
agenda.goal: Confirm the venue numbers and the catering order

agenda.title: Budget check
agenda.goal: See where we are against the budget and what to cut

beats.summary: Carmen inflates the RSVP count; Nina pushes back on new invites
Numbers for the venue and the catering order; Nina's taco truck idea
Where the money is; a quote misremembered; the DJ fight
Shuttle seats, hotel rooms and timing; a schedule mix-up gets corrected

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Can everyone hear me? Leo, you're frozen.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: No, I'm here, I'm here, the camera's just being weird.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Okay, listen, listen, we have a lot to get through, so the guest list first.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: Mom, can we please keep it to the list this time.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: I am keeping it to the list! So we have a hundred and fifty yeses already, that's wonderful.

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: Per the spreadsheet it's a hundred and twelve confirmed.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: That can't be right, everybody I talk to is coming.

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: Everybody you talk to isn't the same as everybody who's sent the card back.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: And we invited a hundred and sixty total, so a hundred and fifty would be wild anyway.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Dude, people always say yes in person and then never RSVP.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: So who hasn't sent it back?

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: Mostly Dad's side, and the cousins in Phoenix.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: The Phoenix cousins always do this.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: To be fair the Phoenix cousins don't check their mail. Like, ever.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: When's the deadline again?

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: May fifteenth.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: That's so soon!

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: Which is why we're talking about it, Mom.

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: I'll text every Phoenix cousin individually tonight and get a yes or no.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: Thank you. Seriously.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: And then the church group. I was thinking we could—

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: Mom, no. We talked about this.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Just a few of them! Marisol and her husband, and the Ortegas.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: That's how it started last time and it turned into forty people.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: No for sure, church people travel in packs.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: That is not a nice thing to say about my friends.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: I'm saying it with love!

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: Okay but, does adding the Ortegas actually fit under the venue limit?

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: The Ortegas are very small people.

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: Mom. The venue seats a hundred and forty, it's not about how much room they take up.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: Maybe we just say no plus-ones for anyone we haven't met?

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: You can't do that to people, it's rude.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: It's kind of normal now, though.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: Fine, let's think about it and come back to it.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Somebody should really call Tía Lupe about her plus-one, she's been asking.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Okay, the venue. Dani, what did we pay them already?

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: The deposit was four and a half thousand.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: That's a lot for a deposit.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Everything is a lot, mijo, it's a wedding.

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: And the catering is sixty-eight a head, so the headcount really matters.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Sixty-eight? I thought they said fifty-five.

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: That was the buffet price. We went with the plated dinner.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Because the plated dinner is elegant.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: Can I just float something? What if we didn't do the plated dinner at all?

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: What would people eat, air?

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: A taco truck. Two, maybe. People love it, and it's way cheaper.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: At a wedding? Your grandmother would—

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: Grandma would love a taco truck, Mom, she literally goes to one every Sunday.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Dude, this is the best idea anyone's had so far.

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: Okay but, has anyone asked the venue if outside food trucks are even allowed?

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: They won't allow it, a place like that.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: My buddy did that at a winery and it was totally fine.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: I actually emailed them yesterday. They allow it with a fee.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: You emailed them without telling me?

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: I'm the bride, Mom. I'm allowed to email my own venue.

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: How much is the fee?

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: They didn't say yet, they said they'd send a sheet.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Speaking of Grandma, did you hear about her hip?

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Wait, what happened to her hip?

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: She was dancing at the Garcias' anniversary and she went down like a tree.

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: Is she okay?

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: She's fine, she's fine, but now she says the doctor is too young to know anything.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Classic Grandma. She told my doctor he looked twelve.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: Okay, can we, the catering. We need to tell them something this week.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Fine. We keep the plated dinner for now.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: For now. I'm not dropping the taco truck.

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: I'll call the venue tomorrow and get the food truck fee in writing.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: And then we vote?

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: There's no vote, I'm paying for a lot of it.

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: Per the spreadsheet, that's not quite true either, Mom.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Okay, the budget. How bad is it?

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: Not bad yet. Total budget is thirty-two thousand, and we've committed about two thirds.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: I thought we said thirty-five.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: It was always thirty-two, Mom. Thirty-five was your number, not ours.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: My number is a perfectly good number.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Sorry, sorry, my cat just walked across the keyboard.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: Hi, Mango.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Okay, so, the DJ. I got the quote back and it's like twelve hundred.

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: The quote you sent me says eighteen hundred, Leo.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Oh. That's, okay, yeah, eighteen hundred. I was thinking of the other guy.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: Eighteen hundred for a DJ?

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Honestly, my band could do it for way less. Like, basically free.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: Leo.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: What! It's a good band!

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Is this the band that played at the quinceañera?

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Different drummer now. Much better drummer.

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: Okay but, are we booking the DJ or not? The quote expires Friday.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: I want a DJ. I love you, Leo, but I want a DJ.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Maybe the band does like one set during cocktails?

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: That could be nice, actually.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: Fine. We book the DJ at eighteen hundred, and Leo's band plays the cocktail hour. Done.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Yes! Okay, I'll book the DJ myself today and send Dani the contract.

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: Thank you. Band at zero dollars, noted.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Zero is harsh.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Zero is generous.

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: Has anyone figured out what we do if the RSVPs blow past the venue limit?

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Listen, the flowers. The florist wants a final count of centerpieces.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: We should probably cut the flowers back, they're a huge chunk.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Weddings need flowers, mija.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: Weddings need people, Mom. Flowers are optional.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Okay, last thing, the day itself. Leo, the shuttle.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: So the shuttle has forty-eight seats booked, and it does two runs from the hotel.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Two runs is enough?

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Two runs covers basically everyone who isn't driving.

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: And the hotel block is twenty-five rooms.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Twenty-five. Half of Phoenix is going to need a room.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Somebody needs to sort out parking for the older relatives, too.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: Half of Phoenix hasn't RSVP'd, Mom.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Wait, what time does the ceremony actually start? I told the shuttle three.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Three o'clock, like always.

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: It's four. It's been four since we booked the venue.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Oh no. Okay. Okay, that's fixable.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: Leo.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Fine. I'll call the shuttle company tomorrow morning and move both runs an hour later.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: And it's still Saturday the ninth, right? Nobody moved the date while I wasn't looking?

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: August ninth. Nobody moved anything.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Good. Your uncle already booked his flights.

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: Do we need a rain plan for the ceremony? It's outside.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: The venue has a tent option. It's an extra cost, though.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Then we get the tent. I'm not watching my daughter get married in a storm.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: Mom, it's August.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: August has storms!

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: Okay. We're going with the tent. Final.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Who's doing the welcome speech at the dinner?

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Okay, I think that's everything. I love you all. This is going to be beautiful.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: Love you, Mom. Thanks everyone.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Peace!

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: Bye, everyone.
